defect_a_bind9_initialisation.witness: bind9 lib/isc/tls.c:88 calls OPENSSL_init_ssl(OPENSSL_INIT_ENGINE_ALL_BUILTIN | OPENSSL_INIT_LOAD_CONFIG, NULL); authority returned 1, candidate returned 0 with 078C0105 (ERR_LIB_CRYPTO/ERR_R_INIT_FAIL), aborting bind9's configure test
defect_a_bind9_initialisation.minimal_reproduction: runtime::init::tests::init_engine_all_builtin_with_load_config_succeeds_like_the_authority, before the source fix: left: 0, right: 1
defect_a_bind9_initialisation.root_cause: src/runtime/init.rs kept OPENSSL_INIT_ENGINE_RDRAND/_OPENSSL/_CRYPTODEV/_CAPI/_PADLOCK/_AFALG on INIT_UNSUPPORTED. OPENSSL_INIT_ENGINE_ALL_BUILTIN is the union of those seven bits, so bind9's option word tripped the refusal before the config step. The authority's ossl_init_engine_* bodies (crypto/init.c:312-380) each return 1 unconditionally; refusing the bit was a return-value divergence, not a faithful refusal.
fix: removed INIT_UNSUPPORTED and both refusal blocks from OPENSSL_init_crypto

runs the engine steps at the authority's coordinates (crypto/init.c:652-682): engine_dynamic keeps its landed loader; the absent loaders (openssl, rdrand, devcrypto, padlock, capi, afalg) are successful no-ops
added the authority's ENGINE_register_all_complete() for OPENSSL_INIT_ENGINE_ALL_BUILTIN (crypto/init.c:685-688)
recorded the retained contents divergence: no built-in engine is registered for the absent loaders (docs/DECISIONS.md D565; src/engine/eng_all.rs)
LOAD_CONFIG unchanged: DEFAULT_CONF_MFLAGS carries CONF_MFLAGS_IGNORE_MISSING_FILE, and def_load maps the BIO missing-file reason to CONF_R_NO_SUCH_FILE; a new init_* test fixes this
preserved: error codes unchanged; ERR_R_INIT_FAIL still raised for the terminal after-cleanup case

defect_b_runtime_libraries.witness: charybdis, memcached and nsd dropped from L7 to L4 under both subjects with libltdl.so.7 and libevent-2.1.so.7 unresolved at launch
defect_b_runtime_libraries.root_cause: forensics/tools/downstream_runtime.py built the launch root only from recipe['aux_sources']. The S64 registry expresses these dependencies as recipe['capabilities'], which bl._prepare_aux extracts into the same <family work>/aux/root, but _aux_runtime_lib_dirs/_aux_runtime_bin_dirs and the harness build environment never read the capability specs. The libraries were therefore present in the build root and absent from LD_LIBRARY_PATH at launch.
fix: new _aux_runtime_specs(recipe) merges capability bundles (bl.deps.resolve_recipe + merge_specs) with legacy aux_sources in the same order _prepare_aux uses
_aux_runtime_lib_dirs and _aux_runtime_bin_dirs now consume the merged specs, so <aux>/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu precedes the subject prefix in LD_LIBRARY_PATH
the workload build environment (CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG_PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH) also consumes the merged specs
_runtime_row records the resolved {capability, bundle_id, sha256} aux_bundles, the same evidence shape the build/link row uses

registry_expression.mechanism: the registry component 'runtime' records the SONAME and path; each package's library_dirs names the extracted directory the launch root must carry. No bundle required re-authoring and no atlas row was restored.
registry_expression.dlopen_limit: the registry can only supply files it pins in a bundle's package set. A consumer that dlopens a SONAME absent from its declared capability still cannot be served by this mechanism; that gap would have to be expressed as a new component, not inferred at launch. No such gap occurred for these three families.
